name: touch_controls
description: Controls drawn on the screen for a touch screen: buttons that stay pressed while a finger is on them, and a stick that gives two axes. They read the fingers as the actions touch_down, touch_x and touch_y (the first finger) and touch_down2, touch_x2, touch_y2 (the second) up to the fourth, which the game's input.json binds to touch:down, touch:x and touch:y of the same names; and they give their own actions to the game, which never learns that a finger did it.

components.name: TouchButton
components.description: A rectangle of the screen, width by height pixels and centred on the entity's Position (put an transform2d.Anchor on it to keep it in a corner). While a finger holds it, the action named by action is 1 (pressed on the tick the finger lands, released when it lifts), and the entity's Sprite shows cell pressed_frame instead of normal_frame. A finger belongs to the first control it lands on or slides onto, and keeps it until it lifts, even if it slides off. finger (the finger that holds the button, 0 for none) and was_held are written for you.

components.name: TouchStick
components.description: A stick: a finger that lands within zone pixels of the entity's Position (a square of side 2 * zone) takes it, and while it stays down action_x and action_y are its offset from the Position divided by radius, kept within [-1, 1] and 0 inside dead_zone (a fraction of the radius). Sprites of the stick and its knob show with their opacity (0 to 255, as a Sprite's alpha). Down is positive y, as on the screen. An action left out is none. The entities with a TouchKnob of the same group follow the finger, at most radius pixels from the Position. finger and was_held are written for you.

components.name: TouchKnob
components.description: The thumb of a stick: an entity that the TouchStick of the same group moves to follow its finger, and puts back on the stick's Position when the finger lifts.

systems.name: follow_fingers
systems.description: Gives the fingers to the buttons and sticks, and their actions to the game, before the simulation ticks. Shows their sprites (alpha = opacity) on a mobile host and from the first finger seen on any other, and hides them until then, so a game for a computer is not cluttered.
